_comment: The lifter's whole black frame — side rails, cross members and the front truss down to the fork hubs — was fused into the chassis mesh (part 11 is one 308k-tri shell, so no connected-component split was available). Carve it out along the arm and hand it to modelWeapon. Two boxes: the beam that runs above the deck, and the truss that dives to the fork ahead of the chassis nose.
Fork hubs (5, 15) and the claw's axle boss (6) rode with the chassis. All three are bolted to the lifter and swing with it.

The carve region also swept up a few of the CHASSIS's own blue livery rails, which then swung with the arm. They are not in a box you can draw around them, but they are unmistakably body-coloured, so select on hue and hand them back. Matching on hue rather than a fixed RGB matters: the same paint in shadow is a fifth of the brightness.

The carve line through a 300k-tri scan shell leaves loose specks of the donor behind, and they swung with the arm as tiny islands out at the far left and right of it. They are not describable by position or by colour — they are simply everything not attached to the lifter frame. The frame is 63391 tris and the front truss 5210; the next largest island is 285, so 400 splits them cleanly.

MEASURED axles. The lifter turns about the boss pair (parts 8/13) at the back of the arm's rear web: centres [-0.246,-0.097,0.085] and [-0.229,-0.106,-0.084], so the axle line is [-0.237,-0.101] on the centre plane. The drop's [-0.05,-0.16,0] was neither.

The claw turns about part 6, the small boss at the base of its stub: centre [-0.1385,-0.044,0.133], taken back to the centre plane. The drop's y of 0.14 was the claw's bbox mid-height — a fifth of the model above its real knuckle, so the jaw flew off its mount.
